title: The 'Swifty effect' set to attract largest TV audience ever for the Super Bowl - as popstar's boyfriend Travis Kelce heads out for star appearance
text:
By Caroline Graham in Los Angeles
Published: 01:00 GMT, February 9, 2025 | Updated: 14:01 GMT, February 9, 2025
Today’s Super Bowl is expected to attract its largest television audience in history, thanks to the ‘Swifty effect’.
The biggest event in American sport sees Kansas City bosses chasing their third consecutive super bowl against Philadelphia Eagles.
Taylor Swift’s boyfriend, Travis Kelce, plays for the Chiefs and his appearance in the game last year led to a record of 123.7 million viewers, with a 24 percent increase in women aged 18 to 24 years.
An NFL source, the governing body of American football, said: ‘The Swifty effect has been remarkable.
‘Every time Kansas City plays, they receive record numbers from the crowd and attract young fans who had never shown interest before.
“We hope that the figures to see for this year’s game are the largest so far and that is completely due to the fast effect.”
On Friday, Mrs. Swift and Mr. Kelce were seen having dinner at New Orleans, where today’s event takes place.
Taylor’s appearance in the game last year led to a record of 123.7 million viewers, with a 24 percent increase in women from 18 to 24 years.

Many expect Kelce to propose to the singer.
The spectators at home will receive the most expensive ads of the Super Bowl with most of the 30 -second slots that cost between $ 10 million and $ 20 million.
Meg Ryan and Billy Crystal received $ 2.5 million each to recreate their famous ‘False Orgasm’ scene in New York for a Hellman mayonnaise commercial.
David Beckham and Matt Damon paid $ 2 million to star in an advertisement for Stella Artois Beer and chef Gordon Ramsey won $ 1 million to plug the Hexclad brand.
